test_title: PYST 42: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I - GA (Held On: 23 Jun, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: According to 2011 census of India, which of the following states/union territories was observed as absence of tribal population?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Punjab**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• As per the 2011 Census of India, Punjab was reported as the state with **no Scheduled Tribe (ST) population**.
 
• This is attributed to the fact that during the reorganization of states in 1966, **tribal areas in Punjab** were allocated to other regions such as Himachal Pradesh.
 
• In contrast, other states like Odisha, Maharashtra, and Kerala have **significant tribal populations**, with Odisha being one of the states with the highest tribal populations in India.
 
• The absence of Scheduled Tribes in Punjab is a unique demographic feature when compared to other Indian states and union territories.
 
• Scheduled Tribes (STs) are officially recognized groups under the Indian Constitution, entitled to specific affirmative actions and reservations.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Tribal Population in India:**

 
 
• India is home to 705 officially recognized Scheduled Tribes, which constitute around 8.6% of the total population (Census 2011).
 
• The tribal population is concentrated in states like Odisha, Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, and parts of the northeastern region.
 
 
 
• **Constitutional Provisions for Scheduled Tribes:**
 
 
• Article 342 of the Indian Constitution empowers the President to specify Scheduled Tribes in states and union territories.
 
• Tribal populations benefit from reservations in education, employment, and political representation under the Fifth and Sixth Schedules of the Constitution.
 
 
 
• **Census of India 2011:**
 
 
• The 2011 Census provided detailed demographic data, including the distribution of Scheduled Castes (SCs) and Scheduled Tribes (STs) across states and UTs.
 
• The tribal population was recorded as 10.43 crore, with the highest numbers in states like Madhya Pradesh and Odisha.
 
 
 
• **Punjab's Unique Demographics:**
 
 
• Punjab has a significant Sikh majority population, with other communities such as Hindus and Muslims comprising smaller proportions.
 
• The absence of Scheduled Tribes reflects historical and administrative factors, including state reorganization and geographical distribution.
